subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Time and Work II — pipes and cisterns, combined work, alternating workers
description: Time and Work advanced: LCM method, combined efficiency, alternate days, pipes and cisterns, work and wages.

questions.stem: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish the work?

options.option_text: 7.2 days — LCM method: total work = 36 units; combined rate = 3+2 = 5 units/day; 36/5 = 7.2 days
15 days — simple average of 12 and 18; ignores that rates, not days, add (not this)
30 days — adds the days directly; completely wrong approach to combined work
6 days — underestimates; only valid if both could each do it in 12 days (not this)

questions.explanation: LCM METHOD: LCM(12,18) = 36 units of total work. A's rate = 36/12 = 3 units/day. B's rate = 36/18 = 2 units/day. Combined = 5 units/day. Days = 36/5 = 7.2 days. FORMULA ALTERNATIVE: 1/T = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36; T = 36/5 = 7.2. PYQ: combined work with two workers is the most basic time-work question in IBPS PO/Clerk, SSC CGL prelims.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and Pipe B empties it in 10 hours. If both are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank from empty?

options.option_text: 15 hours — net filling rate = 1/6 - 1/10 = 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15; so 15 hours
8 hours — adds the two pipe times instead of finding the net rate difference
4 hours — treats both as filling pipes; ignores that B is draining the tank
16 hours — slightly off; wrong sign or wrong fraction in the net rate calculation

questions.explanation: PIPE AND CISTERN: filling pipe = positive; emptying pipe = negative. Net rate = 1/6 - 1/10. LCM(6,10) = 30. Net rate = 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15 of tank per hour. Time to fill = 15 hours. EXAM TIP: if net rate is negative (emptying faster), the tank never fills — watch for trick questions. PYQ: pipes and cisterns in IBPS PO/Clerk, SSC CGL, RRB NTPC — 1-2 questions per exam.

questions.stem: A and B together can do a work in 10 days. B and C together in 12 days. A and C together in 15 days. How long will all three together take?

options.option_text: 12 days — uses one pair's combined rate instead of all three pairs together
6 days — underestimates by not accounting for the overlapping efficiency correctly
10 days — simply uses A+B rate; ignores C's additional contribution to the combined rate

questions.explanation: KEY INSIGHT: Adding all three pair-rates: (A+B) + (B+C) + (A+C) = 2(A+B+C). 2(A+B+C) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15. LCM(10,12,15) = 60. = 6/60 + 5/60 + 4/60 = 15/60 = 1/4. A+B+C = 1/8 per day. All three finish in 8 days. PYQ PATTERN: three-person time-work with pairs is a classic IBPS PO mains-level question; always add all three pair equations.

questions.stem: A does a work in 20 days. A and B together finish it in 12 days. If A works for 9 days and then leaves, how many more days does B need to finish the remaining work?

options.option_text: 12 days — A completes 9/20 in 9 days; remaining 11/20; B alone does 1/30 per day; 11/20 / (1/30) = 11x30/20 = 16.5 days
16.5 days — B's rate = 1/12 - 1/20 = 5/60 - 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30; after A leaves (day 9), remaining = 11/20; B needs (11/20) x 30 = 16.5 days
11 days — confuses remaining fraction with the number of days needed for B (not this) instead however alone
20 days — uses A's full time instead of computing B's rate separately (not this) instead however alone too

questions.explanation: STEP 1: B's rate = 1/12 - 1/20 = 5/60 - 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30 per day. STEP 2: Work done by A in 9 days = 9 x (1/20) = 9/20. STEP 3: Remaining work = 1 - 9/20 = 11/20. STEP 4: Days for B = (11/20) / (1/30) = (11/20) x 30 = 330/20 = 16.5 days. VERIFICATION: A(20 days total) + B(1/30 per day for 16.5 days) = 9/20 + 16.5/30 = 9/20 + 11/20 = 1. PYQ: A leaves early, find B's remaining time — standard IBPS PO prelims question.

questions.stem: A and B work on alternate days starting with A. A can finish the work alone in 10 days, B alone in 15 days. In how many days is the work completed?

options.option_text: 12 days — work in 2-day cycle = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6; 5 full cycles = 5/6; day 11 (A) does 1/10 = 1/10; total 5/6+1/10 = 25/30+3/30 = 28/30; day 12 (B) does enough
10 days — uses only A's rate; ignores B's contribution on alternate days (not this) instead however alone too
11 days — stops one day early; the 28/30 on day 11 is not yet complete (not this) instead however alone too
15 days — uses only B's rate; ignores A's contribution on alternate days (not this) instead however alone too

questions.explanation: ALTERNATE DAY METHOD: Every 2 days: A does 1/10, B does 1/15. Work per 2-day cycle = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. 5 complete cycles (10 days) = 5/6 work. Remaining = 1/6. Day 11 (A's turn): A does 1/10. Remaining after day 11 = 1/6 - 1/10 = 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. Day 12 (B's turn): B does 1/15 exactly. Work finishes at END of day 12. Total = 12 days. PYQ: alternate day work is a medium-hard IBPS PO prelims question.

questions.stem: Three taps A, B, C can fill a tank in 6, 8, and 12 hours respectively. A and B are opened for the first 2 hours, then A is closed and C is opened. How long does it take to fill the tank completely from the start?

options.option_text: 5 hours — first 2 hours: A+B fill 2x(1/6+1/8) = 2x7/24 = 7/12; remaining 5/12 filled by B+C at 1/8+1/12 = 5/24 per hour; time = (5/12)/(5/24) = 2 hours more; total = 4 hours
4 hours — first 2 hours: A+B fill 7/12; remaining 5/12; B+C rate = 1/8+1/12 = 3/24+2/24 = 5/24; time for remainder = (5/12) / (5/24) = 2 hours; total = 2+2 = 4 hours
3 hours — undercounts the remaining work after A closes at hour 2 (not this) instead however alone too
6 hours — uses only one tap's rate for the entire duration incorrectly (not this) instead however alone too

questions.explanation: PHASE 1 (hours 0-2): A+B open. Rate = 1/6 + 1/8 = 4/24 + 3/24 = 7/24 per hour. Work done in 2 hours = 2 x 7/24 = 14/24 = 7/12. PHASE 2: A closed, C opened. B+C rate = 1/8 + 1/12 = 3/24 + 2/24 = 5/24 per hour. Remaining work = 1 - 7/12 = 5/12. Time for phase 2 = (5/12) / (5/24) = (5/12) x (24/5) = 2 hours. TOTAL = 2 + 2 = 4 hours. PYQ: two-phase pipe problems appear in IBPS PO mains quant section.

questions.stem: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. After 6 days, 6 men leave. How many more days are required to finish the remaining work?

options.option_text: 24 days — remaining work after 6 days = 2/3; 6 men at original rate take 2/3 x 36 = 24 days
18 days — uses original 12-man time; ignores the reduction in workforce
12 days — halves the remaining time without adjusting for reduced workforce
36 days — uses 6-man total duration without subtracting the 6 days already completed

questions.explanation: TOTAL work = 12 men x 18 days = 216 man-days. Work done in 6 days (by 12 men) = 12 x 6 = 72 man-days. Remaining work = 216 - 72 = 144 man-days. With 6 men: days needed = 144 / 6 = 24 days. ALTERNATIVE: rate approach: 12 men in 18 days → 6 men would take 36 days for the full job. In 6 days, 12 men complete 6/18 = 1/3 of work. Remaining = 2/3. For 6 men: (2/3) x 36 = 24 days. PYQ: men leave mid-work problems are very common in IBPS PO/Clerk, SSC CGL.
